extracted.intended_audience: Wellcome-funded researchers, research administrators, open-research advocates and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the operating standards and evaluative criteria for Wellcome Open Research's model of immediate publication followed by invited post-publication peer review, including editorial checks, reviewer roles, transparency practices, and indexing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate publication + invited post-publication peer review (model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wellcome Open Research uses a model of immediate publication followed by invited, post-publication peer review. All reviews are citable and posted to the platform along with the identities of the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles are published after editorial checks; reviewers are then formally invited to review the already-published article so they can 'focus their efforts on providing help and advice on how the article can be improved, as well as highlighting any errors or omissions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial pre-publication checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submission is subjected to a range of editorial checks prior to publication, such as plagiarism detection, checking the data availability statement, and ensuring that the appropriate ethical standards have been adhered to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any issues identified during these checks must be addressed before the article is published. These checks are operational prerequisites to immediate publication on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism detection is one of the explicit editorial checks applied to submissions before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism detection is used as a gatekeeping step to identify problematic overlaps before articles appear on the platform; specific tools/processes are not detailed on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial checks include checking the data availability statement for each submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring appropriate data availability supports reproducibility and is part of the pre-publication checklist; issues with data availability must be resolved prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical standards compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are checked to ensure that the appropriate ethical standards have been adhered to before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring ethical compliance is a mandatory pre-publication check; the page indicates this as a criterion but does not enumerate particular ethical policies or documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-suggested reviewers (author-initiated peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: On WOR the reviewers are suggested by the corresponding author and then formally invited to review the already-published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: authors are often best placed to suggest reviewers. Risk mitigation: transparency (signed reviews) and conflict declarations are used to reduce the risk of authors suggesting biased reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conflict of interest declaration and staff checks
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers are required to declare any associations with the author(s). F1000 staff also seek to identify obvious conflicts, such as checking PubMed to determine if any authors have collaborated recently with the reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict declarations are publicly visible (since reviews and identities are posted). Staff perform additional checks (e.g., PubMed searches) to identify recent collaborations as part of managing potential conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review transparency (signed, citable reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review reports are published on the platform and are citable; the identities of reviewers are posted alongside their reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform operates on the principle that transparency ('sunshine is the best disinfectant') will minimise risks from author-suggested reviewers and encourage accountable, substantive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer outcome categories (approval statuses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers indicate whether the work as presented should be 'approved', 'approved with reservations' or 'not approved.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers provide a narrative plus one of the three status indicators. These statuses feed into downstream indexing decisions and provide a lightweight standardized assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing criteria for PubMed and bibliographic databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Only submissions that receive two 'approved' statuses or one 'approved' and two 'approved with reservations' are indexed in PubMed and other bibliographic databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit, operational threshold for a submission/version to achieve indexed status; it defines how many and which reviewer outcomes are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning and repeated peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can submit a new version of the article to address reviewer comments or to update the publication in light of new findings; the peer review process is repeated for each new version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each new version undergoes the same invited post-publication peer review process, and the distribution of approval statuses for version 2 (and later) is tracked separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer role and focus (improvement-oriented reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the research has already been published openly on the platform, reviewers can focus on providing help and advice on how the article can be improved, as well as highlighting any errors or omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model emphasizes constructive, improvement-oriented reviewing rather than acting solely as a gatekeeper prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical metrics on review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported statistics from the first 14 months: for Version 1 articles, of 385 reports 244 were 'Approved', 132 'Approved with reservations', and 9 'Not Approved'. For Version 2 reports (75 total): 69 'Approved', 5 'Approved with reservations', 1 'Not Approved'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcome proportions are presented as evidence of reviewers' willingness to be critical despite author-suggested reviewers and transparency; they can serve as benchmarks for the platform's review behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruitment effort metric
rubrics_metrics.description: To reach indexed status the platform on average approached 11 reviewers; the median number of reviewers contacted to achieve indexed status is nine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operational metric quantifies the effort required to secure the needed approvals and indicates that reaching indexing typically requires contacting multiple potential reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-completion metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis showed that on average articles completed the entire publication workflow in 72 days (analysis conducted in November 2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a benchmark for the elapsed time from initial submission through editorial checks and post-publication peer review to indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of acceptable outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: WOR provides a platform for publishing any research finding that a Wellcome-funded researcher wishes to share, including traditional research articles, data notes, protocols, method papers, software tools and null and negative results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inclusive scope is intended to improve research communication and reproducibility by allowing publication of diverse research outputs beyond traditional articles.
